chapter: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
title: Luis Russell recordings of 1929-30
summary: Asked about Jersey Lightning and other titles, he repeats that his first record was the Oliver date with Russell's band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: - you started to work with Louis Russell's band. You talked about some of the people who were in Louis Russell's band.
How long did you stay with that band?
I know you were with him in '29 because I came to see you in Saratoga, the Saratoga Club.

When you were with Louis Russell's band you made a record that you let me hold the other day - 1929, 1930, Louis Russell - 'Jersey Lightning.' Do you remember some of those songs - Jersey Lightning, Feeling the Spirit, Doctor Blues, 'New' Call of the Freaks? Tell us something about it.
I don't know nothing to tell you...

There were a lot of musicians who were on those records. Can you recall when you recorded those records? When you were in the studio with Louis Russell's band it must have been a big thing for you. Wasn't this one of the first recordings that you had made?

The first recording I made was with Louis Russell's band but it was supposed to have been King Oliver's band. But King Oliver couldn't play and Louis Metcalf played. That was the first record I made with Louis Russell.
What was the name of that song?
That wasn't Your Telephone Number, was it?
